source.prompt: How do I connect a CRM to Gmail and calendar so nothing has to be entered twice?
source.note: real collected answer; brand, competitors and publishers are the specs the cycle was scored with

answer.text:
Connecting your CRM to Gmail and Google Calendar so data syncs bi-directionally (preventing double entry) usually involves one of three main paths, depending on your CRM and tech stack.
Here is how you can set it up, ranked from easiest to most flexible:
Native CRM Integrations
Name: Built-in Workspace Sync
How it works: Most major CRMs (like HubSpot, Salesforce, or Pipedrive) have official, one-click extensions or native settings for Google Workspace. Once authenticated, emails sent from Gmail log to the CRM contact automatically, and meetings booked or scheduled in Google Calendar sync instantly to the deal or contact timeline.
Actionability: Check your CRM's marketplace or settings panel for a "Google Workspace" or "Gmail Integration" toggle and follow the OAuth login prompts.
Third-Party Automation Platforms
Name: Zapier or Make
How it works: If your CRM doesn't have a robust native sync or you want custom behavior (e.g., only sync calendar events with a specific keyword like "Client"), you can build an automated workflow. A trigger like "New Event in Google Calendar" creates or updates a "Record in CRM."
Actionability: Explore pre-made automation templates on Zapier or Make to connect your specific CRM to Google Apps without writing code.
Dedicated Email/Calendar Sync Tools
Name: Cronofy, Nylas, or専用 Sync Add-ons
How it works: For enterprise setups or niche CRMs, specialized calendar and email sync engines sit between Google and your database to handle real-time, conflict-free bi-directional updates.
